subject: BYOK handoff & rotation safeguards for AtlasCloud private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <security@atlascloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AtlasCloud onboarding: BYOK handoff for private deployment

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As we finalize network and deployment windows for the Redwood private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge instances), security has requested a short written plan for BYOK handoff and rotation:

- What Redwood expects AtlasCloud to provide during initial key handoff (format, transport channel, verification).
- The rotation cadence you recommend and how automatic rotation coexists with our compliance needs (we need 90-day rotations but also an operator-driven emergency rotation path).
- How audit logs are captured for key unwrap/sign operations and preserved for 1 year.

Can you assign a couple of folks on your side to draft this? We are aiming to have the artifacts to present to our InfoSec committee by Mon 23 Feb.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Security, AtlasCloud
security@atlascloud.com

Subject: Re: AtlasCloud onboarding: BYOK handoff for private deployment

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in our PM/ops and crypto leads (Vivek and Mina) and Marcus (networking) to put together a short handoff package and a rotation/runbook.

High-level commitment from Redwood:
- We support BYOK via encrypted key-wrap files (PKCS#7 or CMS) delivered over an SFTP endpoint we will provision on your VPC peering subnet, or via a signed envelope to your customer-managed HSM (KMIP session support).
- We'll provide a transfer checklist + verification steps (audit hashes + signer identity) and a one-time verification ceremony (mutual signing + timestamped audit bundle).
- Rotation: default automatic rotation policy is configurable; we can set a scheduled rotation at 90 days and also expose a manual "operator rotate" API for emergency rotations. Automatic rotations are performed by Redwood's rotation service which issues a new data-encryption-key (DEK) wrapped by the customer's KEK (BYOK) and records the event in the audit log.

We'll assemble a 1–2 page handoff document, a rotation-playbook draft, and a network diagram. Attaching the draft artifacts for initial review (see attachments). Will schedule a short sync if you'd like a walkthrough.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm preferred transfer channel (SFTP on peered subnet OR direct KMIP session).
2) Vivek/Mina/Marcus — please add the technical details + verification steps to the attachments and call out emergency/unseal procedures.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud onboarding: BYOK handoff for private deployment

Alex / Hannah — adding the operational constraints we've seen for on-prem BYOK + HSM integrations. Keeping the checklist pragmatic.

Key points:
- Transport: prefer an SFTP endpoint on a peered management VPC with IP allowlist + mTLS client cert for the Atlas transfer agent. If Atlas requests a live KMIP session into their HSM, we will accept a temporary, read-only KMIP binding for initial wrap verification (no unseal performed by Redwood).
- Key formats: recommend RSA-4096 or AES-256 wrapped keys in CMS/PKCS#7; include SHA-256 digest in the envelope metadata.
- Verification: Redwood will return a signed verification token containing a hash of the received KEK and a timestamp signed by our HSM's signing key. Atlas must validate the token locally.
- Audit: rotation and key unwrap events are written to append-only audit stream (immutable storage) and forwarded to Atlas's SIEM over a TLS connection (syslog+TLS). Logs are retained for 1 year by default; extended retention can be negotiated.

Emergency/unseal flow (high level):
1) Operator triggers emergency rotate API (requires 2-of-3 operator approvals via our console or signed requests).
2) System generates new DEK, wraps with the current KEK and the new KEK (if applicable), and performs atomic key swap across replicas.
3) All unwrap/usage events during the window are recorded and a forensics bundle is created (audit + snapshot).
4) If KEK needs to be revoked, an offline key-ceremony is required — Redwood will coordinate a manual rollover and provide signed attestation.

Notes/risks:
- Network path must be low-latency for KMIP sessions; otherwise prefer batched wrapped key exchange.
- Ensure your HSM firmware supports the signing key profile we will use for verification tokens (I can send the exact spec).

Vivek
Senior Systems Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alex — quick draft of the rotation/playbook attached. Key mechanics and operator checklist below (excerpt):

Rotation-playbook (excerpt):
- Scope: DEK rotation (per-model data-encryption keys) wrapped by the customer KEK. KEK lifecycle managed by Atlas (BYOK).
- Scheduled rotation: default 90d; can be reduced to 30d for higher-sensitivity workloads.
- Manual emergency rotation: requires 
  - operator_a approval (CLI signature),
  - operator_b approval (console MFA + audit confirmation).
- Verification steps post-rotation: sanity-run of a small traffic slice, KV cache warmup, and a pre-flight check that verifies all replicas can unwrap the new DEK.

Operator checklist (for emergency):
1) Notify stakeholders via dedicated incident channel.
2) Take pre-rotation snapshot of config and audit stream.
3) Trigger operator_rotate endpoint with 2 approvals.
4) Validate unwrapping of sample objects on each replica.
5) Close incident and push for audit export.

I'll attach rotation-playbook-v1.md with a fuller checklist and some sample CLI commands. Also included a short template for the attestation artifact that Redwood will sign and pass to Atlas on each rotation.

Attachments: rotation-playbook-v1.md

—Mina
Lead, Crypto Ops

Thanks — this is helpful. Two follow-ups from our side after an internal review: 

1) Escrow / emergency unseal: our compliance team wants an additional escrow option for catastrophic recovery (in case Atlas's HSM becomes irrecoverable). We prefer a multi-party escrow where an audited key share is stored with a third-party custodian. Is Redwood willing to accommodate a signed, split-escrow export (threshold shares) as part of the handoff?

2) Evidence for the verification token: we need the exact signing algorithm and certificate chain you'll use so our auditors can validate the attestation.

If you can answer these in writing and provide the updated artifacts, we'll take them to our InfoSec committee tomorrow.

Alex

Alex — appreciate the quick review. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Split escrow: Redwood supports a split-escrow model as an optional add-on for Private deployments. Implementation notes:
- We can produce a threshold-export (Shamir 3-of-5 by default) where shares are split across (a) Atlas custody, (b) Redwood-retained encrypted share in a sealed vault, and (c) third-party custodian (we partner with SafeHSM Inc. for custody operations). Each share movement is logged and attested.
- Escrow exports are only allowed after a documented approval flow (signed request + 2 executive approvals) and will be timeboxed and revocable.
- We will provide an escrow-handback checklist and a signed attestation artifact for every escrow event.

2) Verification token / signing algorithm: our HSM uses ECDSA P-384 with SHA-384 for attestation signing; the certificate chain will be provided as a PEM bundle. We will export a CA-signed attestation certificate and the public verification key in the handoff package.
